issue.mint_text: Mo · Mexico City (right of the bust)

new.story: A Mexican one peso from 1975, carrying Jose Maria Morelos, the priest who became a general of Mexico's independence war and was executed for it in 1815. His portrait faces left under the words UN PESO; the other side shows Mexico's national emblem, the eagle with a snake in its beak standing on a cactus — the sign the Aztecs were told to look for when founding their city. Mexico struck this peso, in copper-nickel, through the 1970s and into the early 1980s, and it jingled in every pocket and bus fare in the country. The little Mo beside the portrait is the Mexico City mint's mark, one of the oldest mints in the Americas.
new.notes: Both sides photographed in the holder. Obverse: UN PESO down the left rim, Morelos facing left, the Mo mint mark right of the bust, and the date below the bust read digit by digit in an enlarged crop as 1-9-7-5 (the 9 is battered but its closed loop and tail are clear; 7 with its flat top bar; 5 with flat top and belly). Reverse: ESTADOS UNIDOS MEXICANOS around the eagle, snake and cactus. The Morelos peso of 1970-1983 is the only Mexican 1 peso of this portrait and metal; earlier Morelos pesos are smaller silver-era pieces and the later 1980s peso changed both portrait style and size.
